project.name: TOOLOR
project.repositoryState: Code is on GitHub and currently deployed to Netlify.

userGoal: Move the public TOOLOR website from its current Netlify deployment to a company-owned computer that should operate as a server, and make it available to all customers through the domain.
importantContext: The user has remote access to the company computer through AnyDesk.
The user is new to hosting a site on a local/on-premises computer.
The company believes the computer may already be configured for 1C and CRM systems, but nobody has provided deployment/network access details.
Do not disable Netlify or change production DNS until the on-premises deployment is working and verified.
AnyDesk is remote-desktop access only; it does not make the computer publicly accessible as a web server.

The current project uses mock commerce data. Cart is local to the browser and checkout does not submit real orders or accept payments. It can be deployed as a storefront/demo, not yet as a production transactional shop.
repositoryFindings: The app is server-run Next.js, with `next build` and `next start`; no static-export configuration was identified.
Architecture documentation states that `https://toolorkg.com` is only a provisional canonical metadata base and final host/migration policy must be confirmed.
Product imagery is served from external URLs.
agreedDeploymentApproach: First perform a read-only infrastructure audit of the company computer and network.
Only then decide whether to use an existing web server, public IP plus router port forwarding, or a secure tunnel such as Cloudflare Tunnel.
Do not open port 3000 directly to the public internet. A production setup needs a reverse proxy (for example Caddy), HTTPS, firewall rules, and automatic restart after reboot.

pendingUserActions.purpose: Identify the host and Windows version.
Identify the operating system and version.
Find the internet-facing IP address visible externally.
Check whether common web/process services already exist.
pendingUserActions.command: sc query type= service state= all | findstr /I "caddy nginx apache iis node pm2"

pendingUserActions.purpose: Check whether a website or local application is already served on the normal HTTP and Next.js development ports.
pendingUserActions.instructions: On the company computer, open http://localhost and http://localhost:3000 in a browser; capture a screenshot of anything that opens.

privacyAndSafety: Do not send passwords, AnyDesk session codes, 1C credentials, router credentials, or private company data into chat.
If sharing the external IP is sensitive, redact it (for example: 185.XX.XX.XX).
Do not change router settings, firewall rules, DNS records, or existing services until the audit results are understood.
nextAssistantTask: Review the audit outputs. Determine whether there is an existing web server, whether the machine is on Windows, whether a public IP and router access are available, and provide an exact safe deployment sequence tailored to the results.
